chunks: Ali b. Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Qazwini, known as Ibn Muqbara, narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abdullah al-Hadrami narrated to us. He said: Jundal b. Waliq narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Umar al-Mazini narrated to us from Abbad al-Kulaybi from Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from Ali b. al-Husayn from Fatima al-Sughra from al-Husayn b. Ali from his mother Fatima bt. Muhammad (blessings of Allah be upon them all). She said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came out to us on the eve of Arafat and said: Indeed, Allah the Blessed and Exalted has dignified and forgiven you all in general, and Ali in particular. I am the Messenger of Allah to you and I am not one who favors his relatives. This Gabriel informs me that the truly happy one, the completely happy, the genuinely happy, is the one who loves Ali in his lifetime and after his death; and that the truly wretched one, the completely wretched, the genuinely wretched, is the one who hates Ali in his lifetime and after his passing.

key_terms.السعيد: The happy/fortunate one - a person blessed with divine felicity
key_terms.الشقي: The wretched/unfortunate one - a person destined for misery
key_terms.جبرئيل: Gabriel - the archangel who brought revelation to the Prophet
key_terms.عشية عرفة: Eve of Arafat - the evening before the Day of Arafat, the holiest day of Hajj
key_terms.محاب: One who shows favoritism - the Prophet clarifies he is not favoring Ali out of nepotism

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about loving and hating Ali on the eve of Arafat?
ai.summary: This hadith is narrated through the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt going back to Lady Fatima al-Zahra (AS) herself. She reports that the Prophet (SAWW) came out to the family on the eve of Arafat -- the most sacred day of the Hajj pilgrimage -- and made a public declaration that Allah had forgiven the believers generally but singled out Ali (AS) for special distinction. The Prophet then invoked Gabriel as his witness to emphasize that true happiness (sa'ada) is tied to love of Ali both during his life and after his death, while true wretchedness (shaqa) is tied to hatred of Ali. This is one of many fadail (virtues) hadiths establishing the spiritual rank of Imam Ali (AS).
